sentences.text: Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by the injured-claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by the judgment & award dated 22.04.2021 passed in MVC No.609/2019 on the file of the III Addl. Sr. Civil Judge & AMACT., Ranebennur (for short, 'Tribunal').
3. Heard.
4.

entities.text: III Addl. Sr. Civil Judge & AMACT., Ranebennur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel Sri.Girish S.Hulmani appearing for the appellant-claimant would submit that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing disability of the injured- claimant at 2%.
As his 4th toe of right leg is amputed, the Doctor has opinioned disability at 7%, however, the Tribunal has considered only 2% which is required to be re-assessed.
He further submits that the award of compensation on all other heads is also on the lower side.

Thus, he seeks for NC:
2024:KHC-D:11487 reassessment of the compensation amount appropriately by allowing the appeal.

5. Per contra, learned counsel Sri.Subhas J.Baddi appearing for respondent No.2/Insurance Company supporting the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal submits that the appellant is working in a private job and even after the accident he continued to work in the same job, hence,
the question of enhancement of compensation would not arise.
He further submits that the Tribunal taking note of the guidelines has assessed the disability at 2% which is in consonance with law.
Further he submits that award of compensation by the Tribunal on all heads is just and proper, does not call for interference.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.
6. I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and meticulously perused the appeal papers along with material available on record.
7. Insofar as disability is concerned, the Tribunal has recorded detailed findings at paragraph Nos.41 and 42 and has assessed the disability at 2%.

Taking note of the prevailing guidelines, I am of the considered view that the disability NC: 2024:KHC-D:11487 assessed by the Tribunal is just and proper, does not call for any modification, however, the award of compensation by the Tribunal Hanumantha B. entities.text: Hanumantha B. S/O. Basavarajappa vs Sri. Mallappa O. S/O. Ningappa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 under the head of pain and suffering, loss of amenities and other heads are on lower side.

Taking note of the same, this Court is of the considered view that it would be just and proper to award enhanced compensation globally at the rate of Rs.50,000/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. Thus, the claimant shall be entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,80,420/- as against Rs.1,30,420/- awarded by the learned Tribunal.

9. In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,80,420/- as against Rs.1,30,420/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
The compensation amount carries interest at 6% P.A, from the date of petition to till payment.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11487 c) The Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today.
d) On such deposit, the same shall be released in favour of the appellant/claimant.
e) Registry to transmit the records, if any, forthwith to the Tribunal.
f) Draw modified award accordingly.

Sd/-
